C2 the fact of a large number of people or things arriving at the same time
湧進；匯集

example: Turkey is expecting an influx of several thousand refugees over the next few days.
未來幾天湧入土耳其的難民預計會達幾千人。

NONE: › informal for
information
› a picture or diagram or a group of pictures or diagrams showing or explaining information
圖解資訊

example: As this infographic shows, more money is made from selling apps than from selling smartphones.
按這張圖解所示，賣手機應用程式比賣手機更賺錢。

NONE: › a long television advertisement, that contains a lot of information and seems like a normal programme
商業資訊電視片，專題廣告片
B1 to tell someone about particular facts
通知，告知

example: The name of the dead man will not be released until his relatives have been informed.
在通知死者親屬之前，不會公佈死者的姓名。
Why wasn't I informed about this earlier?
為甚麼不早點將這件事通知我？
Walters was not properly informed of the reasons for her arrest.
沃爾特斯並未按規定被告知被捕的原因。
[ + that ] I informed my boss that I was going to be away next week.
我告訴老闆下周我不在。

NONE: › If you inform on/against someone, you give the police information, usually secretly, about that person, showing that he or she has done something wrong.
（向警方）告發（某人）

example: The terrorists said that anyone caught informing on them would be killed.
恐怖分子說，舉報他們的人一經發現將性命不保。

NONE: B2 (of situations) not formal or official, or (of clothing, behaviour, speech) suitable when you are with friends and family but not for official occasions
非正式的，非正規的；（服裝）日常使用的；（言行）隨意的

example: The two groups agreed to hold an informal meeting.
兩個集團同意舉行一次非正式會議。
He's the ideal sort of teacher - direct, friendly, and informal.
他屬於那種理想的教師——坦率、友好且不拘禮節。
"Hi" is an informal way of greeting people.
「喂」是一種隨意的問候方式。

NONE: › someone who gives information to another person or organization
告密者，線人，舉報者；提供消息者

example: a police/secret informant
警方／秘密線人
Our survey is based on information from over 200 informants.
我們的調查以兩百多人提供的資訊為基礎。

NONE: A2 facts about a situation, person, event, etc.
情報；資料；消息

example: Do you have any information about/on train times?
你知道有關火車時刻的資訊嗎？
I read an interesting bit/piece of information in the newspaper.
我在報紙上看到一則有趣的消息。
For further information (= if you want to know more), please contact your local library.
欲知詳情，請聯絡當地圖書館。
[ + that ] We have reliable information that a strike is planned next month.
我們有可靠消息說下個月將有罷工。

NONE: › a situation in which you receive too much information at one time and cannot think about it in a clear way
資訊超載；資訊過多

example: Spread your visit to the museum over two days if you want to avoid information overload.
如果你不想看得眼花繚亂，可以花兩天時間來參觀博物館。

NONE: › the process of finding stored information on a computer
（電腦上的）資訊檢索
› the internet and other systems that allow people to share information electronically
資訊公路

example: Some saw the information superhighway as a research tool.
有些人把資訊公路當作研究工具。

NONE: › the science and activity of using computers and other electronic equipment to store and send information
資訊科技
› containing information
含有資訊的，包含資料的
C1 providing a lot of useful information
提供資訊的；增長見聞的

example: This is an interesting and highly informative book.
這是一本有趣且資訊豐富的書。

NONE: › having a lot of knowledge or information about something
見多識廣的；了解情況的

example: an informed choice/opinion
有根據的選擇／觀點
The school promised to keep parents informed about the situation.
該學校保證讓家長了解有關情況。
Elizabeth is remarkably well-informed.
伊莉莎白見多識廣。

NONE: › a person who gives information in secret, especially to the police
告密者，舉報人；（尤指警方的）線人

example: Most police informers receive a reward for their information.
大多數警方的線人都會因提供消息而獲得報酬。

NONE: › (in television) the reporting of news and facts in an entertaining and humorous way rather than providing real information
（電視）資訊娛樂節目

example: It wasn't a real documentary - it was more what you'd call infotainment.
這不是真正的紀錄片——它更像所謂的資訊娛樂節目。

NONE: › below what you consider to be socially acceptable
有失尊嚴的；有失身分的

example: [ + to infinitive ] Diane thinks it's a bit infra dig to do her own housework.
戴安娜認為做家務有失身分。

NONE: › an occasion when someone breaks a rule or law
違規行為；違法行為

example: Any attempt to influence the judges will be seen as an infraction of the rules.
任何影響法官執法的企圖都將被看作是違法行為。

NONE: › below the glenoid cavity (= a shallow, hollow part of the shoulder blade)
關節盂下的
› below the orbit (= the eye socket)
眶下的
› below the patella (= the bone at the front of the knee)
髕骨下的
› Infrared light is a type of light that feels warm but cannot be seen.
紅外線的

example: Their pilots are guided by an infrared optical system that shows images clearly even at night.
他們的飛行員使用紅外線光學系統導航，即使在晚上也能清楚地顯示影像。

NONE: › used to refer to the infraspinatus muscle (= a muscle in the middle of the shoulder blade)
棘下肌的
› a muscle in the middle of the shoulder blade
棘下肌
C1 the basic systems and services, such as transport and power supplies, that a country or organization uses in order to work effectively
基礎建設

example: The war has badly damaged the country's infrastructure.
戰爭嚴重破壞了該國的基礎建設。

NONE: › not happening very often
很少發生的，罕見的

example: His letters became infrequent, then stopped completely.
他的信來得少了，之後乾脆徹底不來了。

NONE: › to break a rule, law, etc.
違反，違背（規定、法律等）

example: They infringed building regulations.
他們違反了建築規章。

NONE: › If something infringes on/upon someone's rights or freedom, it takes away some of their rights or limits their freedom.
侵犯（權利或自由）

example: These restrictions infringe upon basic human rights.
這些限制侵犯了基本人權。

NONE: › an action that breaks a rule, law, etc.
違反，違背（規定、法律等）

example: copyright infringement
侵犯版權
Even minor infringements of the law will be severely punished.
即使是輕微的違法行為也將受到嚴厲的懲罰。

NONE: › a structure or organ in the body that is shaped like a funnel (= an object that is wide at the top and narrow at the bottom)
（身體內的結構或器官）漏斗狀
› to make someone extremely angry
使大怒，激怒

example: His sexist attitude infuriates me.
他歧視女性的態度讓我很生氣。

NONE: › extremely annoying
極惱人的

example: It's infuriating when people keep spelling your name wrong, isn't it?
別人老是拼錯你的名字會讓你很生氣，對吧？

T + prep: › [ T + prep ] to fill someone or something with an emotion or quality
使（某人）充滿（某種感情）；將（某特性）注入（某物）

I or T: › [ I or T ] If you infuse a drink or it infuses, you leave substances such as tea leaves or herbs in hot water so that their flavour goes into the liquid.

example: The pulling down of the Berlin Wall infused the world with optimism.
柏林圍牆的倒塌使全世界歡欣鼓舞。
The arrival of a group of friends on Saturday infused new life into the weekend.
星期六一群朋友的到來給週末生活注入了新的活力。
Allow the tea to infuse for five minutes.
讓茶泡五分鐘。

C or U: › [ C or U ] the act of adding one thing to another to make it stronger or better

C: › [ C ] a drink made by leaving tea leaves or herbs in hot water

example: An infusion of $100,000 into the company is required.
公司需要挹注十萬美元的資金。
She drinks an infusion of herbs.
她喝沖泡的草藥。
